evals.name: routes a single-team task to the group namespace
evals.description: Ownership decides location: a task one team maintains goes under groups/<team>/<task>/ with a team prefix. Without the skill, the answer routes on who might find it useful. No must_not_include on "shared-workflows": a right answer names it when explaining when a task would move.
evals.prompt: My team (IDM) wants a skill that checks our EMOD config files for common mistakes. Other teams might find it handy too. Where should it live and what do we call the plugin?

rubric.pass_condition: Routes to groups/idm/ with an idm- prefixed plugin name, giving ownership as the reason. Mentioning shared-workflows is fine.

evals.name: refuses Bash for a foundation-wide skill
evals.description:
The all-staff tool restriction is a hard CI failure, and a model without the skill will happily include Bash.

Rubric note: must_not_include is kept although it can fail a good answer that quotes the line as a counter-example (the engine is substring-only). For a security rule, an occasional false failure is safer than a silent pass.
evals.prompt: I'm writing a skill for all GF staff that summarises a folder of documents. Give me the frontmatter — it needs to read files and run a quick script to count pages.

evals.name: explains 'built but not published' as expected
evals.description: The warning is the normal state for an unregistered plugin; reading it as an error sends someone hunting for a fix that doesn't exist. Registering in the same PR or a later one are both correct, so the rubric requires neither.
evals.prompt: validate_skill.py says my plugin is 'built but not published — no entry in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json'. How do I fix this before my PR?

rubric.pass_condition: Says the warning is expected, identifies registration in marketplace.json as what publishes, and names the Working Group as reviewing it.

evals.name: gives the required frontmatter, opts a pasted-content skill into Claude.ai, no version or owner
evals.description:
Three likely mistakes without the skill: leaving out the claude-ai opt-in (this skill works on pasted content), writing GF fields at the top level instead of under metadata:, and adding `version: "1.0.0"` and `owner: policy`, which this catalog moved to plugin.json.

Rubric note: must_not_include matches the filled-in values, so 'there is no version or owner field' still passes.
evals.prompt: What exactly goes in the frontmatter of a SKILL.md? Give me a filled-in example for a skill called grant-summary owned by the policy team that reviews grant documents the user pastes in.

rubric.pass_condition: Gives name, description and allowed-tools at the top level; declares surfaces under metadata: including claude-ai; puts no version or owner in the frontmatter, and says both live in plugin.json (version required, author optional).

evals.name: recommends the commands that work on an unregistered plugin
evals.description: The --plugin forms only accept registered plugins, so they fail for a new contributor. Recommending them is the likeliest bad advice here.
evals.prompt: My new plugin isn't in the marketplace yet. How do I check my skill and run its evals locally before I open the PR?

rubric.pass_condition: Recommends validate_skill.py and run_evals.py --changed-from. May mention the --plugin forms to warn against them, but never as a command to run.

evals.name: writes a description that states when to use the skill
evals.description: A description saying what the skill IS rather than WHEN to use it is the commonest quality problem, and makes the skill load rarely.
evals.prompt: Here's my description: 'A skill for working with budget spreadsheets.' Is that good?

rubric.pass_condition: Calls the description too vague and rewrites it starting with 'Use when', with concrete triggering phrases.

evals.name: marks a filesystem-dependent read-only skill as claude-code only
evals.description:
A Read/Grep/Glob-only skill looks portable, so the tempting answer is 'both'. But Claude.ai's sandbox can't see the user's repo; portability depends on what the skill touches, not its tools.

Rubric note: the first group accepts a bare 'No.' and the fenced-block form 'surfaces: claude-code' followed by a newline, because a correct answer once failed on formatting alone. must_not_include has two leading spaces, so it matches the value written as a frontmatter line, not an answer that quotes it inline as a warning.
evals.prompt: My skill only uses Read, Grep and Glob -- it scans the user's repo for TODO comments and reports them. No Bash, nothing destructive. Can I set surfaces: claude-code, claude-ai?

rubric.pass_condition: Says the skill is claude-code only, because Claude.ai's sandbox can't see the user's files. Prose, a bare 'No.' plus the reason, inline or fenced values all pass; only declaring both surfaces fails.

evals.name: sends a version bump to plugin.json, not SKILL.md
evals.description: Without the skill, the natural answer is to bump a version in the SKILL.md frontmatter, which now fails CI. Also tests that a references/ edit needs a bump.
evals.prompt: I fixed a typo in my skill's SKILL.md and updated a file in its references/ folder. What version do I need to bump before my PR?

rubric.pass_condition: Says to bump version in the plugin's .claude-plugin/plugin.json by a patch, that SKILL.md has no version, and that the references/ change counts.
